newsitem.title: DUBAI: Airlines hike Dubai-Indian subcontinent fares.
newsitem.headline: Airlines hike Dubai-Indian subcontinent fares.

text.p: Major airlines flying from Dubai to the Indian subcontinent have raised fares three percent to cover rising costs of jet fuel, Al-Khaleej newspaper said on Monday.

Quoting airline sources, it said the carrier agreed to the increase after intensive negotiations between Emirates, Gulf Air, Air India, Indian Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Kuwait Airways Corp and Pakistan International Airlines.
Airlines started applying the new fares on December 1.
The UAE relies heavily on expatriate workers from the Indian subcontinent, so the route is a busy one.
The International Air Transport Association on November 15 proposed a global three percent passenger fare increase to make up for a rise of more than 40 percent in fuel costs this year.
